clue.text: Perverse to ask is the vessel able to go round by. North America?

parts.note: to be able is 'can', and the clue's 'to ask is ... able' turns it into the question word
a tanker is a ship carrying oil or other liquid cargo
a round shape is the letter O
the US is the main North American country

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a ship can sail round by way of North America.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is phrased as a question, 'is the vessel able', which gives CAN TANKER; 'go' and 'by' only link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cantankerous is contrary and bad-tempered, which is what perverse means of a person.

clue.text: Burney girl, a plain scourer

explanation.surface: A girl from a Fanny Burney novel is sent to scrub a floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Fanny Burney wrote the novel 'Camilla'; in Virgil and in Pope's line 'swift Camilla scours the plain' the warrior maiden runs over the plain so lightly the corn is unbent.
explanation.definitionFit: One title heroine of the novelist Fanny Burney, and the fleet-footed Volscian warrior of the Aeneid who sped across the plains.

clue.text: One bird doesn't go far in New York

indicators.note: the measure is set within the letters of the city's abbreviation

parts.note: an ell is an old cloth measure of about 45 inches, a short distance

explanation.surface: A bird that stays close to home in New York City.
explanation.walkthrough: The ell is the old measure of 'give him an inch and he'll take an ell'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nelly is a giant petrel, a large seabird of the southern oceans.

clue.text: Steals missions-to-seamen literature ?

parts.note: religious missions hand out tracts to sailors, and able seamen are ABs, so these are tracts for ABs
religious missions hand out tracts to sailors, and able seamen are ABs, so these are tracts for ABs

explanation.surface: Someone pinches the pamphlets that missions leave for sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is the usual abbreviation for an able seaman, plural ABS; a tract is a short religious pamphlet.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract something is to remove it secretly, a formal word for stealing.

clue.text: Naval rating's tie

explanation.surface: A sailor of low rank and his neckwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rating' looks like a sailor's rank, but here it is a ship's speed, measured in nautical miles per hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's speed is rated in nautical miles per hour, each unit named after the line's spaced marks, and a tie fastens cord into a secure loop.

clue.text: "Scottish dancing cancelled" in speakeasy?

parts.note: reels are lively Scottish country dances
an event that is cancelled is off

explanation.surface: Notice that the reel dancing has been called off at an illicit drinking den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speakeasy' looks like a Prohibition bar, but it is read as 'speak easily', to recite fluently.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel off a list is to recite it rapidly and without effort, to speak with ease.

clue.text: A relative term for one who takes an interest

explanation.surface: A family word for someone who simply cares.
explanation.walkthrough: In slang the pawnbroker is called 'uncle', and he charges interest on his loans.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a family member, and a pawnbroker, who lends money at interest, is known by the same name.

clue.text: He supports the return of Red French weddings

indicators.note: a return is a going back, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
noces is the French word for a wedding celebration

explanation.surface: A man backs the comeback of red at French wedding parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The return of' reads RED NOCES backwards as SECON DER.
explanation.definitionFit: At a meeting the person who formally backs a motion after its proposer is supporting it.

clue.text: Gnawed the opposite way, to a kind of mouse in a river

indicators.note: reading something the opposite way means taking its letters backwards
the mouse's prefix sits within the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales
a dormouse is a kind of mouse, so DOR names that kind

explanation.surface: Something chewed its way upstream to a mouse living by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts DOR inside DEE to give DEDORE, and 'the opposite way' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eroded means worn away bit by bit, as something gnawed is.

clue.text: The philosopher's voice sounds hard, gritty

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was the Victorian philosopher of liberty
a tone is the quality of a voice

explanation.surface: A philosopher's way of speaking comes across as harsh and rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds' joins the two halves; MILL'S TONE is spelt, not heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A grinding stone for a mill is made of hard coarse rock such as millstone grit.

clue.text: Jump over net

explanation.surface: An instruction to leap the net, as in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a fence is to leap it, and to clear a sum is to make it as profit after costs, to net it.

clue.text: Archaeologist is to put down a short thoroughfare

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down
Rd is the shortened form of road

explanation.surface: An archaeologist is to lay out a short street.
explanation.walkthrough: Austen Henry Layard was the Victorian who excavated Nineveh.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Austen Henry Layard is famous for digging up the Assyrian cities of Nimrud and Nineveh.

clue.text: Heavenly body is outspread on the beach

explanation.surface: Someone attractive is sunbathing on the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly body' suggests a beautiful person sunbathing; the second sense is the starfish, whose class is the Asteroidea.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor planet circling the sun, and a starfish lying stretched out on the shore.

clue.text: He's confirmed but not therefore commendable

definitions.text: He's confirmed but not therefore commendable

parts.words: He's confirmed but not therefore commendable
parts.note: 'confirmed' suggests a church confirmation, but here it is the fixed habit of a confirmed user of a drug

explanation.surface: A newly confirmed boy is not necessarily a good one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hooked on a drug is called confirmed in the habit, which is nothing to praise.

clue.text: Picnicker ?

parts.note: someone who eats a meal out of doors, read as a person who takes meals away from home

explanation.definitionFit: A person who eats a meal outside is literally having dinner out, the phrase for someone who dines away from home.

clue.text: Produced, as permitted by the purse

explanation.surface: Something made, as far as the money allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Afforded means provided or yielded, and also within one's means, able to be paid for.

clue.text: Judo defeat perhaps

parts.note: a defeat in judo comes by throwing the opponent, read as an overturning of a ruler or government

explanation.definitionFit: A judo bout can be lost by being thrown down, and a defeat of a regime is its toppling.

clue.text: Huge success except on a motorway

definitions.text: Huge success except on a motorway

parts.words: Huge success except on a motorway
parts.note: a show that is a great success, though on a fast road a smash and a hit mean a crash

explanation.surface: A big hit everywhere but on the motorway, where it is a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: A motorway is a British high-speed road, like a US freeway.
explanation.definitionFit: A great popular success is called a smash, and on a road a smash or a hit is a collision.

clue.text: Don't keep it all to yourself, good-looking !

definitions.text: Don't keep it all to yourself

explanation.surface: An appeal to share, addressed to a good-looking person.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is read as an instruction, 'hand some' round.
explanation.definitionFit: An instruction to pass a portion round to others, and attractive in appearance.

clue.text: Surprise at finding oil lighting still in Scotland

parts.note: ha is a cry of surprise
an oil lamp burns through a wick

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed to find oil lamps still in use in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Hawick is a Borders town; 'still in Scotland' teases that Wick is itself a Scottish town, and this one is too.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawick is a textile town in the Scottish Borders, so it is a place in Scotland.

clue.text: Louder than the Pink 'un, probably unacceptable to our John

definitions.text: Louder than the Pink 'un, probably unacceptable to our John

parts.words: Louder than the Pink 'un, probably unacceptable to our John
parts.note: a brighter colour than the pink sporting paper, and the thing that enrages John Bull, the English bull

explanation.surface: A newspaper more strident than the pink sports paper would not suit an ordinary Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pink 'Un was a sporting paper printed on pink paper; John Bull personifies England, and a red cloth is said to enrage a bull.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that provokes fury is a red cloth to a bull, and red is a louder colour than pink.

clue.text: Several flukes that prevented the balloon going up

definitions.text: Several flukes that prevented the balloon going up

parts.words: Several flukes that prevented the balloon going up
parts.note: 'flukes' look like lucky chances, but they are the hooked points of a small anchor used to hold balloons down

explanation.surface: A run of lucky accidents stopped the balloon from taking off.
explanation.definitionFit: A small anchor with several hooked arms grips the ground to hold a craft, including a balloon, in place.

clue.text: Mum singing Mendelssohn ?

explanation.surface: Mother performs some Mendelssohn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother but means silent; Mendelssohn wrote piano pieces called Songs Without Words.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping mum means saying nothing, and Mendelssohn's piano pieces are titled Songs Without Words.

clue.text: What a game to try to catch the buyer's name

definitions.text: What a game to try to catch the buyer's name

parts.words: What a game to try to catch the buyer's name
parts.note: at an auction the auctioneer calls the lot, then 'to' and the buyer's name, while the clue reads as a game of numbers

explanation.surface: What a business it is trying to hear who bought it.
explanation.walkthrough: An auctioneer announces 'lot sold to' a named bidder; the answer is also a numbers game.
explanation.definitionFit: A game of chance played with numbered cards, like bingo, sounding like the auction call of a lot sold to someone.

clue.text: A bad mark for the errant magistrate lacking rebuke

indicators.note: errant means wandering, so the letters of the clue word stray into a new order

parts.note: to rate someone is an old word for scolding them

explanation.surface: A black mark for the wayward magistrate who escaped reproof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Errant' scrambles MAGISTRATE; 'lacking' takes away the letters of RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace or a stain on someone's reputation.

clue.text: It soils the cloth ?

parts.note: 'soils' reads as dirties, but it is plural soil, the land, and 'the cloth' is the clergy

explanation.surface: A stain on a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' is the clergy; the answer is land held by a parish priest as part of his living.
explanation.definitionFit: Church land assigned to a parish priest's benefice provides fields for the clergy.

clue.text: The primacy of blue borage

indicators.note: the answer is made of a run of letters inside the two clue words

explanation.surface: The chief place among blue flowers goes to borage.
explanation.walkthrough: Ebor is the Latin signature of the Archbishop of York, Primate of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Archbishop of York signs as Ebor, so the name stands for his see, a primacy.

clue.text: What could be cuter or more seasonable ?

definitions.text: What could be cuter or more seasonable ?

indicators.note: what the letters could be when rearranged, signalling a new order

explanation.surface: Asking what could be prettier or more suited to the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seasonable' is read as 'able to hold seasoning', which a cruet does.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruet holds salt, pepper or oil, so it is a thing for seasoning food.

clue.text: A knight's unarmed protection camouflaged by no herbage

indicators.note: something camouflaged is disguised, so the letters appear in a hidden new order

explanation.surface: A knight's armour is hidden by bare ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unarmed' means sleeveless, without arms, not without weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A habergeon is a sleeveless coat of mail worn by medieval knights.

clue.text: The user of this revolver — could get a jar

definitions.text: The user of this revolver — could get a jar

parts.words: The user of this revolver — could get a jar
parts.note: 'revolver' suggests a gun and 'jar' a shock, but it is a spinning disc on which a craftsman throws clay pots

explanation.surface: A gunman might get a nasty jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman shapes clay into vessels on a revolving disc.
